beats.summary: Dwight insists on standing instead of sitting, claiming health benefits, while others are skeptical or tease him.

evidence.snippet: Dwight: Standing is proven to be healthier, increases productivity and just looks cooler.
Jim: Hey guys let's just all admit it. Ok? Dwight's better than us. He had the guts to stop sitting.

beats.summary: Jim pranks Dwight by taking money from his wallet, leading to a playful confrontation about standing versus sitting.

evidence.snippet: Jim (sees a pole poking out Dwight's pant leg): What are you up to? Oops look out!

Jim: Because you're sitting?
Dwight: Standing.

beats.summary: Robert introduces his wife Susan (Mrs. California) to the office as she considers returning to work.

evidence.snippet: Robert: Everyone. I'd like to introduce my wife Mrs. Robert California.
Susan: Hello. Oh call me Susan please.

beats.summary: Andy is tasked with showing Susan around the office and finding a suitable role for her despite being fully staffed.

evidence.snippet: Robert: Andy would you be so kind as to show Susan around the office.
Andy: I would love to. But I have to be completely honest with you guys. We're 100 percent staffed up.

beats.summary: Dwight opens a gym in the office building to promote health and reduce obesity-related costs.

evidence.snippet: Dwight: Well today's your lucky day. I have opened in this very office building Dwight Schrute's Gym for Muscles.
Dwight: Obese people in my office are a drain on resources.

beats.summary: Andy feels overshadowed as the office is unusually friendly to Susan, his wife's presence causing tension.

evidence.snippet: Jim: I don't know. He wasn't talking to me. But if I were you I wouldn't hire his wife.
